title: Will Europe’s Protests Mark a Turning Point? | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Michael Froman argues the French protests signal a collapse of France's social contract and a looming debt crisis with no escape mechanism, converging with a US pivot toward Russia that exposes Europe's security dependence; he sees a long winter unless Europe fixes structural weaknesses.

insights.claim: France's protests are categorically different from its usual street tradition, stemming from a collapse of the social contract: weak education investment, rising pension spending financed by a shrinking young workforce, anemic growth and affordability pressure.
insights.so_what: French political and fiscal instability may be underpriced.
insights.quote: canary in the coal mine of a broader political and economic crisis
insights.locator: Top of mind are the protests
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: One in five young people in France is unemployed, and the streets are filled with the young.
insights.so_what: Youth unemployment fuels unrest and far-right gains.
insights.locator: Top of mind are the protests
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: France faces a potential debt crisis with no obvious escape: growth is too weak to tax its way out, no party will survive broad spending cuts, and defense spending is committed to double from 2017 levels by next year.
insights.locator: Downstream from breaking the social contract
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: The public sector consumes about 57 percent of French GDP versus 37 percent in the US, and a government-commissioned report says annual interest payments will rise 59 percent by 2030.
insights.so_what: Quantifies the fiscal squeeze behind the borrowing-cost pressure.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: Investors are skeptical France can solve its problems given political sclerosis, pushing borrowing costs higher.
insights.so_what: Expect a risk premium on French debt until reform visibility improves.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: France and the UK both face payments they cannot afford fiscally, cuts they cannot afford politically and spending they cannot ignore geopolitically; the UK has avoided crisis through stronger growth and central bank backstops, tools France lacks, as do Italy and Belgium.
insights.so_what: Euro-area peripherals lack a UK-style backstop.
insights.locator: France and the United Kingdom (UK) both face
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: An ascendant far right in France, heading into the April 2027 election and with Germany's rolling elections, will try to capitalize on the resentment from the protests to implement anti-immigrant agendas.
insights.so_what: Election-driven policy risk in France through April 2027.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: The UK is on its sixth prime minister in ten years and Macron is on his seventh prime minister, illustrating Western democratic dysfunction.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: Trump waived a new bipartisan law imposing secondary sanctions on Russia and cut a deal to buy Russian diesel, and said Russia 'has been fine on Ukraine', bringing the US-Ukraine relationship to its lowest point since the early-2025 Oval Office meeting.
insights.so_what: Sanctions pressure on Russia is weakening; watch Russian diesel flows.
insights.quote: Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine
insights.locator: This is all coming to a head
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: European rearmament is at this stage fundamentally talk and will take years to replace reduced US commitment, so the US remains the only outside power that can meaningfully affect the war's outcome.
insights.so_what: European defense-industrial payoff is a multi-year story.
insights.quote: All the talk of European rearmament is, at this stage, fundamentally talk.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman

insights.claim: The combined economic, political and security pressure may finally push Europe toward Draghi/Letta-style reforms, consolidation of its military industrial base and greater autonomy, though this depends on fixing political dysfunction.
insights.so_what: A reform catalyst is possible but unproven; watch policy follow-through.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
